open_decision: The order of the added rows: no law fixes the order in which the new starter entries are appended after the old rows (a design can also add an entry more than once).
input: config: locked = none, enable = false. registry: [] . starter: [{id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled true}, {id 2, adapter 1, model 2, enabled true}] (distinct ids).
result_a: refSync order: [{id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled false}, {id 2, adapter 1, model 2, enabled false}]
result_b: reversed order of the added rows: [{id 2, adapter 1, model 2, enabled false}, {id 1, adapter 1, model 1, enabled false}]
reason: Law 1 only needs the result to be the old registry followed by some added list. Laws 2 to 6 check each added row alone, and law 3 checks presence only, so the reversed design passes every law. A second run adds nothing for both designs, so law 7 holds too.
